body:
Update: the fallout from 7989608d is systemic, not one test. I ran all JVM test tasks on the PR #10 head (`sbt all …`), which has 7989608d merged onto origin/main; PR #9's CI passed all of these before it.

Same root cause everywhere: independently constructed or read unresolved spaces now get distinct frame ids (e.g. FrameMismatch "scalafim-world:unresolved:e2df03b4bb5c5e2a-17" vs "-18"), so exact congruence and alignment fail.
1. fit ImageMapsSuite:107 (reported above).
2. mvpaSpatial SpatialFeatureSetPlansSuite:97, "volume label maps become regional feature plans with linear voxel ordering": SamplingAlignment.exact(actualD3, expectedD3).
3. archivedResponseInterop LnaDatasetSuite:247, "loads one archive as a LatentArchiveDatasetBackend": Grid.exactCongruence between two reads of the same archive (absolute vs relative path).
4. threshold: two tests (ThresholdCoreSuite geometry-failure expectation, DecisionScaleSuite mask built on a separate SampleSpaces). I own threshold and have fixed both test-side on the PR #10 branch; the code under test was correct in both cases.
5. atlas MniTemplateBridgeFilesSuite timed out after 711 s under the parallel run. I'm re-running it alone to see whether that's load or a real change.

The design question behind all of these: under 7989608d, two reads of the same NIfTI (or of two files with identical geometry) without world evidence are no longer compatible. User workflows are affected, not only tests. For example, threshold's MaskedField requires Grid.exactCongruence(stat, mask), so a stat map and a mask loaded from separate files would now be refused.

Is that the intended STP semantics?
- If yes, the call sites and tests in fit, mvpa-spatial and archived-response interop need migrating: carry the source space through, or admit shared world evidence.
- If no, restore a deterministic identity for unresolved frames with identical geometry, as SampleSpaces.persistentD3 did.

PR #10 cannot merge until you decide. The shared checkout's local main already contains 7989608d, so these failures are live there too.
